question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for older adults compared to regular hospital care?

options.A: Eliminating all signs of natural aging

explanation: Rehabilitation focuses on helping patients regain their independence and adapt to daily life, rather than just curing the disease. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why should a nurse know the difference between normal aging and actual illness?

options.A: It proves that chronic diseases can be completely reversed in old age
options.B: It guides targeted interventions to prevent avoidable functional dependence
options.C: It ensures patients are discharged immediately without follow-up care
options.D: It eliminates the need for multidisciplinary team involvement

explanation: Spotting treatable issues helps nurses plan care that keeps patients as self-reliant as possible. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h1)

question: What areas of life does a Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment look at, besides physical health?
explanation: This assessment looks at the whole person, including mental well-being, daily habits, and social support systems. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why is it important to involve the older adult when setting rehabilitation goals?

options.A: It guarantees that all chronic conditions will be fully cured
options.B: It ensures the targets align with the patient's personal priorities and motivation
options.C: It removes the legal liability of the nursing staff
options.D: It prevents the family from interfering with medical treatment plans

explanation: Patients work harder and stay more motivated when they help choose goals that matter to them. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of restorative nursing care for older adults?

options.A: Preventing functional decline through daily task encouragement
options.B: Providing complete nursing assistance for all daily activities
options.C: Reducing the cost of hospital medications and supplies
options.D: Speeding up the discharge process from the hospital ward

explanation: Restorative care encourages patients to do as much as they can for themselves to prevent muscle weakness from disuse. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h3)

question: An older patient is scared to walk after a mild stroke. What is the best first step?

options.A: Insist that the patient remain on strict bed rest until fully healed
options.B: Delegate the ambulation task exclusively to unqualified family members
options.C: Order a wheelchair and prohibit any future attempts at walking
options.D: Encourage short, supported ambulation sessions using a walking frame

explanation: Taking small, supported steps builds the patient's confidence and keeps their joints flexible. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h3)

question: What term describes the simultaneous presence of multiple chronic diseases in an older adult?
explanation: Multimorbidity refers to having two or more chronic health conditions at the same time. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why are older adults more likely to experience bad reactions to medications during recovery?

options.A: Pharmacies in Nigeria only supply expired drugs to elderly patients
options.B: Chronic diseases make drugs completely ineffective in the body
options.C: Their bodies metabolize and excrete medications differently due to aging changes
options.D: They always refuse to take prescribed medications on schedule

explanation: As the liver and kidneys age, they process drugs more slowly, which can cause medicines to build up in the body. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which nursing intervention uses past memories and experiences to improve psychological well-being?
explanation: Reminiscence therapy involves discussing past life events to promote connection and self-esteem. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h5)

question: What makes spotting depression tricky in older adults?

options.A: It is impossible to treat once the patient reaches eighty years of age
options.B: It only occurs when patients are discharged back to their homes
options.C: It can present as physical complaints and social withdrawal rather than sadness
options.D: It always causes immediate, severe memory loss identical to Alzheimer's disease

explanation: Older adults often show depression through body aches, fatigue, or pulling away from family rather than crying. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which validated tool is commonly used to screen nutritional status in older adults?
explanation: The Mini Nutritional Assessment is designed specifically to identify risk of malnutrition in the elderly. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h6)

question: An older patient shows signs of mild dehydration and confusion. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Wait until the doctor makes rounds before offering any water
options.B: Provide frequent small sips of preferred fluids throughout the day
options.C: Restrict all oral fluid intake to prevent nighttime urinary frequency
options.D: Discontinue all solid foods and rely entirely on tube feeding

explanation: Giving small, regular drinks helps clear up mild confusion and restores fluid balance safely. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is an environmental risk factor for falls in an older adult's home?

options.D: Loose floor rugs and poor hallway lighting

explanation: Things in the surrounding environment, like rugs and poor lighting, are extrinsic risks, unlike body factors. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h7)

question: Which of these actions does NOT help prevent patient falls?

options.A: Conducting regular medication reviews to check for sedating drugs
options.B: Assessing the patient's gait and balance using standard scales
options.C: Installing secure grab bars in the bathroom and toilet areas
options.D: Keeping all patient room lights completely switched off at night

explanation: Pitch-black rooms make it easy to trip and fall when a patient tries to get out of bed in the dark. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h7)

question: Who usually acts as the main person connecting the healthcare team and the family during rehabilitation?
explanation: Nurses spend the most time with patients and coordinate daily care updates between doctors, therapists, and family members. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h8)

question: Why is proper discharge planning important when an older adult leaves a rehabilitation facility?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any further family involvement in care
options.B: It ensures the patient never has to visit a healthcare clinic again
options.C: It transfers all legal responsibility away from the hospital permanently
options.D: It prevents relapse and ensures rehabilitation gains are maintained at home

explanation: A smooth transition plan helps patients keep up their progress at home and avoids sudden hospital readmissions. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h8)
